title: Tileflow responsive density mode for console rollouts and cost explorer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design exploration for a new 'Tileflow' density mode that allows dashboard panels, rollout cards, and cost explorer rows to fluidly compress and expand across breakpoints while maintaining interaction parity across Chromium, Firefox, Safari (desktop and iOS) and legacy Edge. Goals: 1) provide a compact density mode for heavy-data surfaces that preserves readability and keyboard navigation; 2) ensure charts and table canvases reflow without layout jank or offscreen clipping; 3) harmonize modal stacking and gesture handling on touch devices to avoid accidental dismissals; 4) produce a pixel-perfect prototype for handoff to front-end engineering with clear CSS/JS constraints and fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard tile grid switches between spacious / default / tileflow-density on user toggle and via responsive breakpoint (>=1200px, 900-1199px, <=899px)
Charts (sparklines, line, bar) redraw cleanly on container width changes without causing full-page reflow; canvas fallback uses debounced resize and preserved pixel ratio
Tables maintain row height compression but keep focusable controls visible at all breakpoints; horizontal overflow uses condensed column mode with persistent sticky key columns
Modals open and stack correctly on iOS Safari: focus trap works, background scroll lock uses body position fallback, swipe-to-close disabled for critical modals
Cross-browser visual parity: shadows, clipping, and scrollbar behaviors audited and recorded in implementation notes
Prototype in Figma + interactive Zeplin-like prototype (HTML/CSS proof-of-concept) available for engineering handoff
design_notes: Tileflow uses CSS container queries where available, with JS fallback using ResizeObserver for Firefox/Safari versions without full container query support
Use transform: translateZ(0) sparingly; prefer will-change: transform for animated elements to avoid forcing layer promotion across all browsers
Virtualized table rows with dynamic row-height: measure first N visible rows then reuse height cache to avoid layout thrash on fast scroll

Charts: prefer SVG for small sparklines for crispness at low PPI; use canvas for dense time-series where pixel-level control and performance are required. Provide both render paths behind a feature flag

Modal stacking: create explicit stacking index map in CSS variables and avoid relying on DOM order. On iOS, implement body inert + position fixed fallback to prevent rubber-banding affecting modal content
Gesture collisions: disable pointer capture for background overlays; ensure drag handles in panel header consume pointer events only when the handle is targeted
review_feedback: PM (Asha Rao): Ensure the toggle is discoverable in both page-level settings and per-dashboard toolbar; prefer an opt-out for new users rather than opt-in

Eng (Ravi Patel): Concern about ResizeObserver flood on high-frequency resizes; recommend debounced observer and threshold-based redraws. Also call out the need for explicit keyboard focus anchors when rows collapse
Security (Ibrahim S.): No direct security concerns, but request that modals with export buttons log telemetry events for audit tracing
Design Lead (Elena Gomez): Visual density looks good; ask to tighten token spacing variables and produce a compact token set for left-aligned data grids
decisions: Use CSS container queries as primary strategy with ResizeObserver fallback to minimize JS when supported
Provide dual-render chart approach (SVG sparklines, canvas for heavy panels) behind a runtime flag to allow gradual rollout
Implement tileflow as an optional density mode persisted in user prefs and overridden by admin UX for enterprise tenants
Disable swipe-to-dismiss for high-importance modals by default; allow configurable behavior per-modal type
next_steps: Produce final Figma frames for large/medium/small breakpoints and annotate CSS tokens (1 week)
Deliver interactive HTML/CSS proof-of-concept addressing ResizeObserver debouncing and keyboard anchors (2 weeks)
Schedule design+eng sync to review performance instrumentation needs and rollout gating (this week)
Create QA checklist across browsers including macOS Safari/Firefox/Chrome, Windows Edge/Chrome, iOS Safari, Android Chrome
